name: South Dakota
rateNote: Bid-down system — investor accepts lowest rate willing to take
keyNotes: December auction — one annual sale per county
3-year redemption plus mandatory 60-day notice before deed
Low population, rural land heavy — limited inventory
summary: South Dakota holds limited annual lien sales, mostly in December. Certificates are transferable. 3–4 year redemption before deed. Statute: SDCL §10-25.
typeWhy: South Dakota sells tax lien certificates at limited annual sales. The owner retains title during the 3-4 year redemption period. SDCL §10-25.
rateWhy: South Dakota sets a fixed statutory rate of 12% per annum on tax lien certificates. This is a flat, non-auction-determined rate. SDCL §10-25.
notBeginnerReason: Long 3–4 year redemption, limited inventory, December-only auctions.
beginnerTip: Minnehaha (Sioux Falls) and Pennington (Rapid City) counties have the best SD inventory. Note that certificates are transferable — you can sell your certificate position to another investor.
risks: Limited inventory outside Sioux Falls and Rapid City
ddExtra: Calculate opportunity cost over the 3–4 year holding period
Verify the exact redemption period for the county
Confirm certificates are transferable if you need liquidity before redemption

steps: Find your target county treasurer at sd.gov/government/counties
Contact the treasurer in October to confirm a December sale is scheduled

tylerCompliance.summary: Status pending — monitoring for legislative action.
tylerCompliance.details: This state compliance with Tyler v. Hennepin County (2023) is currently being monitored. Aurigen tracks legislative updates, pending bills, and court decisions that affect tax sale surplus requirements. Check back for updates.

rules.statute: SDCL Title 10, Ch. 22 (Delinquent Collection) + Ch. 23 (Sale) + Ch. 24 (Redemption) + Ch. 25 (Tax Deeds)

process.taxes: Taxes paid 1 year in arrears (e.g., 2024 taxes payable in 2025). Due Jan 1; 1st half delinquent May 1, 2nd half delinquent Nov 1.
process.certificate: Tax certificate issued on any property with delinquent taxes. Annual sale.
process.bidMethod: Bid-down INTEREST RATE — treasurer offers tract; bidder states lowest interest rate accepted per year. Lowest bid wins certificate. Treasurer issues Certificate of Sale.
process.countyBid: If no private bidder — county bids for the property (county holds certificate)

auction.frequency: Annual — typically December (contact county treasurer for exact date)
auction.platform: County treasurer — in-person (each of 66 counties independently)
auction.bidMethod: Bid-down interest rate on full amount of taxes, interest, and costs
auction.payment: Certificate holder pays taxes owed immediately; earns bid-rate interest upon redemption

otc.name: County-Held Tax Certificates
otc.process: Contact county treasurer directly. County may assign certificates it holds.
otc.note: SDCL §10-23-25 — county bids off property when no private bidder. Resulting certificate assignable.
otc.statute: SDCL §10-23-27 — all taxes must be paid before county assigns certificate

subTax.name: Subsequent Tax Payments
subTax.note: Certificate holder may pay subsequent taxes. Keeps lien position.

redemption.period: Any time before tax deed is issued — minimum 3 years from date of tax certificate sale (town: 3–6 years; rural: 3–6 years)
redemption.amounts: All taxes + interest + penalties + costs accrued. Must include current taxes if requested by county (SDCL §10-24-7).
redemption.disability: Persons under disability: extended redemption period (SDCL §10-24-3)
redemption.notice: Before applying for tax deed — certificate holder sends formal notice. 60 days from filing affidavit of service = last chance to redeem.

deedPath.name: Quit Claim Deed (Tax Deed) — county issues post-proceedings
deedPath.eligibleAfter: No sooner than 3 years, no later than 6 years from date of tax certificate sale (town and county equally — SDCL §10-25-1)
deedPath.titleEffect: Releases all liens EXCEPT: municipal special assessments (delinquent/current/future), state liens, federal liens. County/mechanic liens, judgments, mortgages, other specials: ABATED.
deedPath.note: Pennington County example: QC deed to purchaser. Any info on IRS/state liens — direct to those governments.

surplus.name: Surplus Proceeds
surplus.statute: SDCL §10-25-12 (implied); SD Dept of Revenue county treasurer guidance
surplus.claimPeriod: 180 days from tax deed sale for prior owner to claim
surplus.afterExpiry: Transferred to Unclaimed Property Division per SDCL ch. 43-41B
surplus.process: Treasurer returns surplus to prior owner of record. If prior owner not found within 180 days — Unclaimed Property.
surplus.note: Tyler v. Hennepin compliant — SD DOR guidance explicitly states surplus returned to prior owner

es.summary: Dakota del Sur realiza ventas de gravámenes anuales limitadas, mayormente en diciembre. Los certificados son transferibles. Redención de 3–4 años antes de escritura. Estatuto: SDCL §10-25.
es.typeWhy: Dakota del Sur es un estado de gravamen porque los condados venden certificados de gravamen fiscal en diciembre con período de redención de 3-4 años. Los certificados son transferibles (SDCL §10-25).
es.rateWhy: La tasa del 12% anual es moderada pero la redención de 3-4 años es una de las más largas del país (SDCL §10-25).
es.notBeginnerReason: Larga redención de 3–4 años, inventario limitado, subastas solo en diciembre.
es.beginnerTip: Los condados Minnehaha (Sioux Falls) y Pennington (Rapid City) tienen el mejor inventario en SD. Tenga en cuenta que los certificados son transferibles — puede vender su posición de certificado a otro inversor.
risks: Redención de 3–4 años es muy larga
Las subastas solo en diciembre limitan el tiempo
Inventario limitado fuera de Sioux Falls y Rapid City
ddExtra: Calcule el costo de oportunidad durante el período de retención de 3–4 años
Verifique el período de redención exacto para el condado
Confirme que los certificados son transferibles si necesita liquidez antes de la redención

steps: Encuentre al tesorero de su condado en sd.gov/government/counties
Contacte al tesorero en octubre para confirmar que una venta de diciembre está programada
Solicite la lista de propiedades en mora
